HEADING INKS MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED: both headings are printed in the same cyan #00adef (flat interior sample, 2828 and 1297 exact-match pixels respectively) - neither is black. Body prose is #221f1f, the footer year is pure #000000. Heading sizes measured individually: '1.2 TAXONOMIC CATEGORIES' is bold serif small caps, full-cap height 24.5 px (y 486-510, baseline 510) = 1.20x body; '1.2.1 Species' is bold serif upper-and-lowercase, cap height 23 px (y 1512-1535, 'p' descends to 1542) = 1.12x body. I mapped the higher-level numbered section 1.2 to role major_heading and the subsection 1.2.1 to section_heading, since the allowed list offers only those two and 1.2 is both larger and higher in the hierarchy. COLUMNS: one column only, but it is NOT centred - the measure runs x 533-1535 px (0.313-0.903), leaving a 31%-wide empty outer (left) margin on this verso page and only a 9.7% inner margin. I verified the left margin carries zero ink below the header (0 dark pixels in x<533, y 210-2080), so nothing is printed there on this page; the column is reported as 'full' because all content sits in the single measure. A renderer that centres the column will misplace every line. INDENTS: no element's left edge is inset from the column, so indent is 0.0 everywhere. However, blocks 4 and 5 each begin with a FIRST-LINE indent of 49 px = 0.029 of page width (first line starts at x 583, all later lines at x 534); blocks 1, 3 and 7 are flush because they are continuations - block 1 runs on from page 5 and block 7 runs on to page 7. I deliberately did not put 0.029 in 'indent' because that field means the whole element is inset, and a renderer would indent the entire paragraph. TWO STACKED HEADER STRIPS: the top of the page carries a tall pale-green block (y 0-178, #e0ebb6) with a thin grey strip beneath it (y 179-206, #d1d2d4) that holds the running head and folio. Both are reported as page_header_band because the allowed-role list has no separate name for the second; they are distinct printed elements with distinct fills. The folio '6' sits in a white rounded tab that protrudes upward out of the grey strip into the green block; I report the tab rectangle (x 217-313, y 143-207) as the page_number bbox because a renderer has to draw it, and the digit itself occupies [0.143, 0.0845, 0.153, 0.0937]. Its space_before is 0.0 because it overlaps the bands above rather than following them. FOOT: the bottom strip is a solid 92 px green band (y 2086-2178, #cadf7f), not a thin rule - footer_rule is the nearest allowed role. The centred sans '2024-25' (y 2082-2098) straddles the band's top edge; I labelled it running_header as the running FOOT, distinct from the serif small-caps 'BIOLOGY' running head at the top right. The last element is the NCERT diagonal watermark '(c) NCERT / not to be republished', a light grey (about #e8e8e8) overlay spanning x 388-1530, y 303-1976 across the body text. It is an overlay with no position in the reading flow - I listed it last and a consumer should drop it. page.fill 0.99: the content fills the measure solid from the first line (y 297) to the last baseline (y 1976) with no slack - no figure, table, box or white gap anywhere on the sheet - and the 110 px below the last baseline is the normal foot margin before the band. There are 39 body lines plus 2 headings. All seven A2 blocks matched to a position with confidence by line counts: block 1 = 4 lines, block 3 = 6, block 4 = 9, block 5 = 9, block 7 = 11; no nulls were needed and no element is unmatched. Elements A2 never blocked (two header bands, folio, both running heads, footer band, watermark) carry n: null. 'face' is reported with the value of the brief's 'font' field on every text element; both keys are emitted because the brief's schema names it 'font' and my instruction named it 'face'. align, text_color, font and face are omitted on the bands and the watermark, which carry no type of their own (brief rule 5: omit rather than guess). One artefact not reported as an element: a 1 px black line at the extreme top-left corner (y 1, x 0-39) - a trim/crop mark from the render, not printed furniture.
